FIGURE 2 | (a) Cross‐section SEM pictures of LICGC. Surface of the 5 nm sample (A) and 10 nm sample (B). Interlayers are on the left side of the sample edge (a very small visible indication for the 10 nm sample only). FIGURE 3 | (a) Sequence from pristine to after several strippings and platings of Li metal: voids form on stripping; lateral growth of a thin Li film across the electrolyte surface (nucleating where void edges meet the electrolyte) on subsequent plating results in low plating polarization and formation of occluded voids. Some voids are eliminated on plating, but the occluded voids reopen on subsequent stripping, leading to accumulation of voiding and increasing loss of contact with cycling. This increases stripping polarization and results in dendrites on plating [59]. Reproduced from [59] with permission from Springer Nature, Copyright 2019. (b) Cl 2p XPS spectra of the cathode before and after cycling: HE‐LIC cell and LIC cell [36]. Reproduced from [36] with permission from Springer Nature, Copyright 2024.
